_comment: Tier-2: IncrementalUpdateStaticSmoothingScheme smooths Cauchy stress to the nodes in FinalizeSolutionStep and therefore needs the full dam_mechanical_solver nodal set — NODAL_AREA, NODAL_CAUCHY_STRESS_TENSOR, NODAL_JOINT_WIDTH, NODAL_JOINT_AREA — even for a purely mechanical static run. Pitfall (kratos.dam #4). Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). The scheme resolves on DamApplication. Its required variables straddle two modules: NODAL_AREA is core, while NODAL_CAUCHY_STRESS_TENSOR, NODAL_JOINT_WIDTH and NODAL_JOINT_AREA are PoromechanicsApplication attributes — not Dam's, and not core's. A user of a Dam scheme has to import Poromechanics to name three of the four. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 INVERTS the expected outcome of all 7 probes -- it asserts the opposite of what this build actually does, while leaving each probe's callable untouched so every probe still really runs against Kratos. Every probe[...] line then disagrees with itself and probe_mismatches goes from 0 to 7. This proves the printed booleans come from actually calling into Kratos on this build, and that a wrong claim is caught, rather than the fixture echoing a hard-coded table. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: all 7 probe[<label>]=<ok>_expected=<must> lines, probe_mismatches=0. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/dam_smoothing_scheme_nodal_set && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
